chunks: And it is narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:
I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man from among the qammāṭīn entered upon him and said: “May I be your ransom.”
Profits, wealth, and trade come into our hands, and we know that your right in them is established, yet we fall short regarding that.
So he عليه السلام said: “We would not have dealt justly with you if we had obligated you with that today.”

key_terms.الْأَرْبَاحُ: profits or gains acquired through economic activity
key_terms.الْأَمْوَالُ: wealth or property in one's possession
key_terms.مُقَصِّرُونَ: falling short in fulfilling an obligation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about claiming his right from profits and trade?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a report to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about gains and trade in which his due is known to exist. The Imam عليه السلام responds by indicating leniency, saying it would not be fair to burden them with that at that time. The narration is significant in discussions of khums and the practical treatment of the Imam’s right in financial gains.
